transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I am here because people keep acting like I am imagining it. But I am not blind, I know for a fact the hospital people and some folks from the agency have been watching our house. They are even keeping tabs on my cleaning routes to see if I am taking proper care of my husband. 

Which is just ridiculous because I take care of everything. I clean houses for a living, you know, I am a housekeeper. Just on Tuesday I was doing a deep clean over on Elm Street, and the lady there has these huge, heavy velvet curtains. You wouldn't believe how much dust they hold. I had to take them down and haul them outside to beat them, and my shoulder has been aching ever since. My husband used to help me with the heavy lifting before he got bad, but now it is just me doing it all. We used to have a beautiful garden, too, lots of tomatoes and squash. The bugs got to the squash this year though... wait, what was I saying? 

Oh, right, why I came in. But yes, they think I am making up the agency people watching my routes, but I know what I see.

When you say the hospital people and agency are watching your house and monitoring your cleaning routes, do you think there might be any other explanation for what you're experiencing, or are you completely certain this is actually happening?

No, no, there is no other explanation. I am completely certain. Like I said, people keep acting like I am just imagining it all, but I know for a fact the hospital people and the agency folks are watching the house. They are monitoring my cleaning routes to see if I am taking proper care of my husband, and I am not blind. 

I mean, I see their cars. Just yesterday, there was a dark blue sedan parked right across from the Miller place—that is my Thursday morning job. Mrs. Miller has this beautiful antique grandfather clock in her front hallway. It chimes every quarter hour, which honestly drives me a little crazy when I am trying to mop the hardwood floors. I use a special oil soap there, and it takes a lot of focus so it doesn't streak. You have to go exactly with the grain of the wood, you know? My mother taught me that. She was an absolute stickler for clean floors. We used to scrub them on our hands and knees every Saturday morning before we were allowed to watch cartoons... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about being sure. Yes, I am absolutely sure they are watching me. I know what I see, doctor.
Besides seeing those cars watching you, have you ever heard voices speaking to you when no one else was around, or seen things that others couldn't explain?

Well, yes, actually. I don't usually tell people this because they look at me funny, but even when the house is completely quiet, I hear a woman's voice. She's usually right near the kitchen window, clear as day, like she's standing right next to me. She tells me to check the locks or move my husband's pills. 

Speaking of the kitchen window, I really need to wash those curtains. They're a yellow gingham, very cheerful, but they catch all the grease from the stove. I usually take them down and soak them in the bathtub with a little bleach and detergent. You wouldn't believe the color of the water that comes out of them. It reminds me of this one time I was cleaning for the Hendersons. They had this massive grease fire in their kitchen—ruined the cabinets, the ceiling, everything. I spent three days just scrubbing the walls with a degreaser. The smell of that stuff... it gives you a headache if you don't open all the windows. And their dog, a little terrier mix, kept trying to lick the soapy water off the floor. I had to keep shooing him away... 

What was I saying? Oh, the voice. Yes, the woman by the window. I definitely hear her, clear as if she's right there.
When did you first start hearing that woman's voice and noticing people watching your house? Did this all start suddenly, or has it been building up gradually over weeks or months?

Well, let me think... it's been going on for a while now. The voices and the feeling that people are watching us, I'd say it's been happening for about 11 months now. 

It started around the same time I was doing that big spring cleaning job for the Petersons. Oh, they have this lovely house, but the dust! You wouldn't believe it. They have these intricate baseboards, you know, the kind with all the little grooves? You can't just run a mop over them, you have to get down with a toothbrush and really scrub. I spent hours on those baseboards. And their cat, Mr. Whiskers, he just sat there watching me the whole time, judging me, I swear. Cats are like that, aren't they? They just stare at you. Reminds me of my aunt's cat, Barnaby. He used to hide under the sofa and swipe at your ankles when you walked by. We had to start wearing thick socks just to go into the living room...

Oh, dear, I lost my train of thought again. But yes, about 11 months, that's how long it's been since the voice and the watching started.

Besides the stress from worrying about being watched and hearing the voice, have you been able to keep up with your housekeeping jobs and take care of your husband and home the way you normally would, or has this all made it harder for you to do those things?

Well, it's... it's definitely made things harder, yes. My cleaning agency actually took away my supervisory routes. They said the clients and my coworkers felt they couldn't rely on my work the way they used to, which is just ridiculous because I am very thorough. I mean, I always make sure to use the right polish on the brass fixtures. You can't just use any all-purpose cleaner on real brass, it tarnishes it terribly. I learned that the hard way when I first started out, working at this old Victorian bed and breakfast. The owner, Mrs. Higgins, she had these gorgeous brass doorknobs on every single door. There must have been thirty doors in that house. I spent a whole afternoon polishing them once, and my hands smelled like metal for two days straight. No matter how much lemon juice and salt I scrubbed them with, the smell just lingered... 

Oh, but you were asking about my husband, weren't you? Yes, well, at home, my husband and our pastor have had to step in a lot more lately. They say I'm not keeping up with the caregiving and the household stuff safely. Pastor Thomas even started bringing over casseroles on Tuesdays. He makes a lovely tuna noodle casserole, though he puts peas in it, and I always pick the peas out. I just can't stand the texture of cooked peas, they get so mushy. But yes, they've been having to help out because things have just been... slipping, I suppose.
When you're talking with someone, do they ever tell you that it's hard to follow what you're saying, or that you jump around between different topics? Does that happen to you often?

Well... yes, I suppose they do. It's very frustrating because it all connects perfectly fine in my head. But when I try to explain what is happening, the words just sort of run away from me. I'll start out talking about my husband's heart pills, and then somehow I'm on about the church schedule, or the numbers on my client list, and people tell me they just can't follow me at all. 

Speaking of the church schedule, they just changed the time for the Sunday evening service, and Pastor Thomas's wife, Brenda, she handles all the printed bulletins. She started printing them on this pale blue paper. It's a nice color, robin's egg blue, but she uses this font that's terribly hard to read. It's all curly and squiggly. I told her, Brenda, the older folks in the congregation can't read this, but she just smiled and said it looked elegant. Elegant! What good is elegant if Mrs. Gable misses choir practice because she thought a three was an eight? Mrs. Gable is a sweet lady, though. She makes the absolute best rhubarb pie for the summer potlucks. I always try to get a slice before it's gone, but her grandson usually eats half the tin himself. He's a big boy, plays football for the high school, so I suppose he needs the calories, but still... 

Oh, dear. I'm doing it right now, aren't I? Jumping around. But yes, people do tell me it's hard to follow what I'm saying.

When you first started noticing the voices and the people watching you about 11 months ago, were you already having trouble organizing your thoughts and jumping between topics the way you do now, or did that confusion with your speech come later?

Well, I... I'm not entirely sure, to be honest. It's hard to pin down exactly when the talking got so muddled. I mean, 11 months ago, that was right around the time I was doing the Petersons' spring cleaning, like I said. And the voices were definitely there then. But the speech thing... I don't know if it started exactly then or a bit later. 

Time just gets away from you, doesn't it? Like how it's already November, and I haven't even thought about getting the winter coats out of the cedar chest. I always keep them in the cedar chest to keep the moths away. Moths are just terrible around here. Last year, they got into my husband's favorite wool sweater, the green one he wears when he goes ice fishing. He was so upset. He loves ice fishing, though I can't understand why anyone would want to sit on a frozen lake for hours. He takes this little thermos of coffee, but it always goes cold by noon. I bought him a new thermos for Christmas, one of those expensive vacuum-sealed ones, but he said it was too heavy to carry out on the ice... 

I'm sorry, what were we talking about? The confusion with my speech... I just really can't say for sure if it started right at the same time as the voices or if it came on later. It's all just a bit of a blur.

When you think back to about 11 months ago when this all started, did the voices and the feeling of being watched come on suddenly—like one day you noticed them and they were just there—or did they start very gradually, getting a little bit stronger or more noticeable day by day?

Well, it's... it's hard to remember exactly how it started. I just don't know if it was all at once or little by little. 11 months ago, that was right before the holidays, and the holidays are always such a rush. You're running around trying to find the perfect gift, and the stores are just packed. I went to the mall to get my husband that thermos I was telling you about, and the line at the register was all the way back to the shoe department. And the shoes they sell nowadays, they just don't have any arch support. I bought a pair of flats for work, and my feet were aching after just two houses. You really need a good, sturdy shoe when you're on your feet all day, especially on hard floors. Tile is the worst for your back. The Petersons have this beautiful Spanish tile in their kitchen, but sweeping it is a nightmare because the dirt gets caught in the grout lines... 

But anyway, about the voices and the watching... I really couldn't tell you if it was sudden or gradual. It's just too hard to remember how it all began.

When you're having a conversation with someone, do they seem frustrated or confused because your thoughts jump around so much, or do they mostly understand what you're saying even though it might take you a while to get to the point?

Well, I think... yes, people definitely get confused. My husband gets so frustrated with me. He'll ask me a simple question and I just... I can't seem to give him a straight answer because my mind is just going so fast. It jumps from the electric bill we need to pay, to those Bible verses Pastor Thomas read on Sunday, to worrying about my husband's breathing when he sleeps—he has this terrible snore, you know, it sounds like a lawnmower starting up. And then I'm thinking about which house I need to clean next, whether it's the Petersons or the Smiths. The Smiths have that awful shag carpet in their den, it's impossible to vacuum properly. You have to go over it three times just to get the dog hair out, and they have this golden retriever that sheds everywhere. He's a sweet dog, though, always brings me his tennis ball when I walk in. I used to have a dog when I was a little girl, a terrier mix named Buster... 

Wait, what was I saying? Oh, right. My mind just jumps so fast between all these things—the bills, the Bible verses, the cleaning schedule—that I just can't catch one thought long enough to finish it before the next one starts. So, yes, I think they do get very frustrated because I can't stay on track.

Before all this started 11 months ago with the voices and the watching, were you functioning normally at work and at home? I mean, were you able to keep your cleaning jobs going smoothly and take care of your husband without any problems?

Well, before the 11 months... oh, yes, I was doing just fine. I was actually a supervisor. But since all this started, my cleaning agency actually took away my supervisory routes. They told me that the clients and my coworkers were complaining, saying they just couldn't rely on my work the way they used to. Which really stung, you know? I used to take so much pride in my routes, especially the ones out by the lake. The houses out there have such massive windows. You need a really good squeegee for those, none of that cheap rubber that leaves streaks. I always bought my own supplies because the agency's glass cleaner smelled like pure ammonia. It gives you such a headache if you're in a closed room with it. I used to get terrible headaches when I was younger, the kind where you just have to lay in a dark room with a cold washcloth over your eyes... 

Anyway, what did you ask? Oh, taking care of things. Yes, at home it hasn't been smooth either. I just haven't been keeping up with the caregiving and my household responsibilities safely. It's been too much. So my husband and Pastor Thomas have had to step in a lot more to help manage things. Pastor Thomas is such a saint. He came over last Tuesday to help sort out the pantry, and he brought this lovely peach cobbler. Peaches are out of season right now, so he must have used canned, but it was still good. I always prefer fresh peaches, like the ones from the farmer's market downtown. They have this one stall that sells the biggest, juiciest peaches you've ever seen, but you have to get there by 7 AM or they sell out completely. I used to go every Saturday morning, back when I had my old station wagon... 

I'm sorry, did I answer your question about work?

Looking back to before the voices and the watching started 11 months ago, when you were working as a supervisor and doing well—did you have this same problem where your thoughts would jump around quickly and people would have trouble following what you were saying, or is that something that only started happening after the voices began?

Well, before the 11 months... no, I don't think so. I don't remember my thoughts jumping around like this back then. I mean, I was a supervisor, you know? You have to be very organized to be a supervisor. You have to keep track of all the schedules, the keys, the alarm codes... Oh, those alarm codes. Some people pick the hardest numbers to remember. The Smiths had one that was, I think, their wedding anniversary backwards, plus the year they bought the house. Who can remember that? I always just write them down on a little notepad I keep in my apron pocket. It's a blue apron, the one with the deep pockets. You need deep pockets for the keys and the extra trash bags. I buy those heavy-duty trash bags, the ones with the red drawstrings, because the cheap ones always tear when you're pulling them out of the can, and then you've got coffee grounds all over the floor. Coffee grounds are terrible to sweep up, they just smear everywhere if the floor is even a little bit damp. My husband drinks that dark roast coffee, French roast, I think. It smells so strong in the morning. He always leaves the mug on the counter instead of putting it in the sink... 

But, um, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, before the voices started, I don't think I had this trouble with my thoughts jumping around. People seemed to understand me just fine back then.

You mentioned that before the voices and watching started 11 months ago, people understood you fine and you were organized as a supervisor. But I want to be very clear about the timing: when you first started hearing that woman's voice by the kitchen window, were you already having trouble with your thoughts racing and jumping around like they do now, or did that speech problem develop later, after the voices had already started?

Well, let me think about that... when I first heard her by the kitchen window... I really don't know which one happened first. I remember being at the sink when she started talking. We have this little bird feeder right outside that window. My husband put it up for the cardinals, but the squirrels always get to it first. They are so clever, you know? They climb right down the wire and hang upside down just to eat the sunflower seeds. We tried putting out that spicy seed, the kind that's supposed to keep them away, but I swear our squirrels actually like the heat. My neighbor, Mrs. Gable, she puts out whole peanuts for the blue jays. Blue jays are so loud, though, they just squawk and chase all the little goldfinches away. I used to love watching the finches while I was washing the dishes. I always use the lemon-scented dish soap, it cuts through the grease on my husband's frying pans so much better... he makes bacon every Sunday morning and the grease just splatters everywhere, all over the stovetop and the backsplash... 

I'm sorry, what were you asking? Oh, about the racing thoughts and the voice. Honestly, Doctor, I really couldn't tell you the exact timing. It's all just a big blur now, so I don't know if my mind was already jumping around when she started talking, or if that came later. It just sort of all jumbled together.
Before you started hearing that woman's voice 11 months ago, did you ever notice your thoughts racing really fast or jumping from one thing to another like they do now, even back then?

Well, before the 11 months... no, I don't think they did. But now... oh, it's just exhausting. My mind jumps so fast from the electric bills to Bible verses, and then I'm listening to my husband's breathing while he sleeps, and then I'm trying to figure out which house I need to clean next... I just can't catch one thought long enough to finish it before another one takes over. 

It's like trying to catch leaves blowing in the wind. We have this huge oak tree in the front yard, and in the fall, the leaves just cover everything. My husband used to rake them into these big piles, and the neighbor's kids would come over and jump in them. They had these little red boots, the kind with the frogs on the toes. I always thought frog boots were so cute. I wanted to get a pair for my niece, but she lives down in Florida, and they don't really need rain boots like that down there. It's mostly just sandals. I bought her these little pink sandals with rhinestones once, but she outgrew them so fast. Kids grow like weeds, don't they? You buy them something, and two months later, it doesn't fit... 

But anyway, what was I saying? Oh, right. No, before she started talking by the window, I don't remember my mind racing like this. It's just so hard to keep track of things now.

I want to make sure I have this right: when you were working as a supervisor before the voices started, and people could understand you just fine—during that time, did you ever feel like your mind was racing really fast, or was your thinking clear and organized back then?

Well, back then, when I was the supervisor, my thinking was very clear. I had to be organized. But now... it's just so fast. Like I said, my mind jumps so fast from the bills to Bible verses to my husband's breathing to which house I need to clean next that I can't catch one thought long enough to finish it. It's just exhausting. 

I was actually just looking at our electric bill yesterday. It's gone up so much since they installed those new smart meters in the neighborhood. The man who came to put it in, he had this bright orange vest on. It was so bright, it kind of hurt my eyes to look at it in the sun. He said it was for safety, which makes sense, I suppose. You want people to see you if you're working near the street. My husband used to wear a reflective vest when he would ride his bicycle in the evenings, but he hasn't ridden that bike in years. It's just sitting in the garage, gathering dust. The tires are probably completely flat by now. I should really ask him to pump them up or just give the bike away. There's a donation center right down by the old grocery store... the one that closed down last year and turned into a discount furniture place. I went in there once to look for a new armchair, but everything smelled like cheap glue and plastic... 

Wait, what did you ask me? Oh, about my thinking back then. Yes, before all this started, my mind didn't race like this. I was very clear and organized.

When you first started hearing that woman's voice by the kitchen window 11 months ago, at that exact time, was your mind already racing fast like it is now, or did your mind start racing fast sometime after you began hearing her voice?

Well, like I was trying to explain... I really don't know which one happened first. When she started talking by the window... I don't know if my mind was already going this fast or if it started later. It's just all a blur. But I do know that right now, my mind jumps so fast from the bills to Bible verses to my husband's breathing to which house I need to clean next that I just... I can't catch one thought long enough to finish it. 

I clean for the Hendersons on Tuesdays, and they have this massive golden retriever. Oh, he sheds everywhere. I have to use the special attachment on the vacuum just to get the hair off the sofa cushions. They have these lovely velvet cushions, deep green, like a pine tree. We used to get a real pine tree for Christmas every year when the kids were little, but the needles would drop all over the carpet and it was just a nightmare to clean up. My husband finally bought a fake one on sale after New Year's... it has the lights already strung on it, which saves so much time. The lights are those tiny white ones, not the big colored bulbs. My mother always liked the big colored bulbs, especially the blue ones. She said the blue ones looked like stars in the snow... 

I'm sorry, what were we talking about? Oh, right, the timing. Yes, I just don't know if my thoughts were racing like this when the voice started, or if it happened after. I just can't remember.

I know this is hard to remember, but let me ask it a different way: in the weeks or months right before you heard that woman's voice for the very first time by the kitchen window, were you already noticing that your thoughts were racing and jumping around quickly like they do now, or was your thinking still clear and organized back then?

Right before? No, I'm pretty sure I was still clear-headed then. I could organize my days and my schedule just fine back then. It's only now that... well, like I keep telling you, it's just a complete mess in my head. I bounce so fast from the bills, to some Bible verse, to just staring at my husband and listening to him breathe, to trying to remember which house I'm supposed to clean next. I just can't hold onto a single thought long enough to actually finish it. 

And my husband's breathing... honestly, it's a wonder I get any sleep anyway because he snores so loudly. He has this old green flannel pillowcase he refuses to throw away, and he just buries his face right into it. I bought him a really nice silk one for Christmas because I read in a magazine that silk is better for your skin and it stops your hair from breaking. The magazine was at the dentist's office. Dr. Miller. He has this huge glass fish tank in the waiting room with these little neon tetras. They just dart around so fast, back and forth, hitting the glass... kind of like my brain right now, I guess. 

But no, to answer your question, before the woman started talking at the window, my thoughts weren't darting around like that. Everything was perfectly normal before all this.

Let me make sure I understand the timeline correctly: about 11 months ago, before you heard that woman's voice for the very first time, were you experiencing this racing, jumping-around feeling in your thoughts at all, or did that racing feeling only start happening after you began hearing her voice?

Like I just said, I don't really know. I can't remember exactly when the racing started. I just know that right now, my mind jumps so fast from the bills to Bible verses to my husband's breathing to which house I need to clean next that I can't catch one thought long enough to finish it. It's just all happening so fast. 

I was trying to read my Bible this morning, actually. The print is getting so small... or maybe my eyes are just getting worse. I went to the optometrist last year, Dr. Chen. He told me I needed bifocals. I hate bifocals. They make me feel so old, and the line right in the middle of the lens gives me a headache. My grandmother wore bifocals. She had these thick, heavy plastic frames that were sort of a peach color. She used to bake the most wonderful peach cobbler in the summer when the peaches were ripe. We'd go out to the orchard and pick them ourselves. The fuzz would get all over my arms and make me itch... 

I'm sorry, I forgot what you were asking me again. Was it about the voice?

I know you've had trouble remembering this, but I want to ask you one more time very simply: in the weeks right before you first heard that woman's voice by the kitchen window, were you able to focus and keep your thoughts organized, or were your thoughts already racing and jumping around like they are now?

Well, right before... yes, I think I was fine before the voice started. I could focus then. But now, when I try to explain what is happening, the words just run away from me. They run from my husband's heart pills to the church schedule to the numbers on my client list, and people say they can't follow me. 

My husband takes those little white pills for his heart, you know. He has to take them twice a day, morning and night. I bought him one of those plastic pill organizers with the days of the week printed on it, but the letters are starting to rub off. The 'T' for Tuesday is completely gone. I clean for the Hendersons on Tuesdays... wait, I already told you about their dog, didn't I? The golden retriever. They are such sweet dogs, but they need so much exercise. My cousin had a golden retriever named Buster who used to dig holes all over the backyard. He dug up all her prize-winning petunias one spring. She was so mad she wouldn't speak to the dog for a week, which is silly because dogs don't understand the silent treatment. They just know when you're upset. They can smell it on you, I think. 

But anyway, people tell me they can't understand what I'm saying because I jump around so much from the heart pills to the church bulletin to my clients... it's just really hard to keep it straight.

When you first heard that woman's voice by the kitchen window 11 months ago, at that exact moment, did your mind feel clear and focused, or was it already racing and jumping around the way it does right now?

Well, at that exact moment... I don't think it was racing. Actually, there was a spell for a few weeks right around then where things were quieter. I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't rushing around from house to house so much. But even when things were quiet and I was resting, I still heard her voice right there by the kitchen window. I still knew the agency was watching us, even if my thoughts weren't going a mile a minute. 

Speaking of the window, I need to wash it. The glass gets so streaky when it rains. I use vinegar and newspaper to clean the windows at the Hendersons' house, it works much better than that blue spray stuff. My mother taught me that trick. She used to save all the Sunday papers just for cleaning. The Sunday paper used to be so thick, full of coupons and the colored comics. I always read the comics first... Peanuts was my favorite. Snoopy sleeping on top of his doghouse... I never understood how he didn't roll off in his sleep. I toss and turn so much at night, mostly because of my husband's snoring, like I told you. If I slept on a roof, I'd fall right off and break my neck. 

But no, my mind wasn't racing then. It was actually one of those quieter spells, but the voice and the agency watching us... that was all still happening.

You've told me that a few weeks after you first heard the woman's voice by the kitchen window, your thoughts started racing really fast. Is that right—the racing thoughts came after the voice started, not before?

Yes, that's right. The racing came a bit after. But you know, during those weeks when my thoughts were just flying and I was barely sleeping at all... I was just running constantly, from my cleaning jobs straight to church errands and back again. And the whole time I was rushing around like that, I was still hearing her voice. I was absolutely certain people were monitoring the routes I was taking between the houses and the church. 

I take Elm Street to get to the church usually, because the traffic lights on Main Street take forever. They put in a new light by the old bakery, and it stays red for what feels like hours. I used to love that bakery. They made these little powdered sugar cookies that melted right on your tongue. My aunt used to buy them for my birthday every year. She passed away last spring, bless her heart. We had her funeral at the same church I do the bulletins for. The flowers were beautiful, mostly lilies. I always think lilies smell a bit too sweet, almost like they're trying to cover something up. But they do look nice against the dark wood of the altar. I have to polish that wood next week... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, yes, the racing thoughts definitely started after the voice. I'm sure of that now.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the racing thoughts and flight of ideas preceded the onset of psychotic symptoms (voices and delusions) or developed concurrently/after, which would help differentiate F20.0 (paranoid schizophrenia with primary psychotic features) from F20.2 (catatonic schizophrenia, though less likely here) or suggest a mood disorder with psychotic features.
doctor.question: I know this is hard to remember, but let me ask it a different way: in the weeks or months right before you heard that woman's voice for the very first time by the kitchen window, were you already noticing that your thoughts were racing and jumping around quickly like they do now, or was your thinking still clear and organized back then?

target_item.name: Racing_Thoughts
target_item.manifestation: My mind jumps so fast from bills to Bible verses to my husband's breathing to which house I need to clean next that I can't catch one thought long enough to finish it.

patient.answer:
Right before? No, I'm pretty sure I was still clear-headed then. I could organize my days and my schedule just fine back then. It's only now that... well, like I keep telling you, it's just a complete mess in my head. I bounce so fast from the bills, to some Bible verse, to just staring at my husband and listening to him breathe, to trying to remember which house I'm supposed to clean next. I just can't hold onto a single thought long enough to actually finish it. 

And my husband's breathing... honestly, it's a wonder I get any sleep anyway because he snores so loudly. He has this old green flannel pillowcase he refuses to throw away, and he just buries his face right into it. I bought him a really nice silk one for Christmas because I read in a magazine that silk is better for your skin and it stops your hair from breaking. The magazine was at the dentist's office. Dr. Miller. He has this huge glass fish tank in the waiting room with these little neon tetras. They just dart around so fast, back and forth, hitting the glass... kind of like my brain right now, I guess. 

But no, to answer your question, before the woman started talking at the window, my thoughts weren't darting around like that. Everything was perfectly normal before all this.

patient.answer:
Like I just said, I don't really know. I can't remember exactly when the racing started. I just know that right now, my mind jumps so fast from the bills to Bible verses to my husband's breathing to which house I need to clean next that I can't catch one thought long enough to finish it. It's just all happening so fast. 

I was trying to read my Bible this morning, actually. The print is getting so small... or maybe my eyes are just getting worse. I went to the optometrist last year, Dr. Chen. He told me I needed bifocals. I hate bifocals. They make me feel so old, and the line right in the middle of the lens gives me a headache. My grandmother wore bifocals. She had these thick, heavy plastic frames that were sort of a peach color. She used to bake the most wonderful peach cobbler in the summer when the peaches were ripe. We'd go out to the orchard and pick them ourselves. The fuzz would get all over my arms and make me itch... 

I'm sorry, I forgot what you were asking me again. Was it about the voice?

doctor.question: I know you've had trouble remembering this, but I want to ask you one more time very simply: in the weeks right before you first heard that woman's voice by the kitchen window, were you able to focus and keep your thoughts organized, or were your thoughts already racing and jumping around like they are now?

target_item.name: Disorganized_Thinking_Speech
target_item.manifestation: When I try to explain what is happening, the words run from my husband's heart pills to the church schedule to the numbers on my client list, and people say they can't follow me.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking whether the patient was able to keep their thoughts organized, which directly inquires about disorganized thinking and speech.

patient.answer:
Well, right before... yes, I think I was fine before the voice started. I could focus then. But now, when I try to explain what is happening, the words just run away from me. They run from my husband's heart pills to the church schedule to the numbers on my client list, and people say they can't follow me. 

My husband takes those little white pills for his heart, you know. He has to take them twice a day, morning and night. I bought him one of those plastic pill organizers with the days of the week printed on it, but the letters are starting to rub off. The 'T' for Tuesday is completely gone. I clean for the Hendersons on Tuesdays... wait, I already told you about their dog, didn't I? The golden retriever. They are such sweet dogs, but they need so much exercise. My cousin had a golden retriever named Buster who used to dig holes all over the backyard. He dug up all her prize-winning petunias one spring. She was so mad she wouldn't speak to the dog for a week, which is silly because dogs don't understand the silent treatment. They just know when you're upset. They can smell it on you, I think. 

But anyway, people tell me they can't understand what I'm saying because I jump around so much from the heart pills to the church bulletin to my clients... it's just really hard to keep it straight.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the patient's racing thoughts and flight of ideas began before or after the onset of psychotic symptoms (voices and delusions), which would help differentiate between F20.0 (paranoid schizophrenia with primary psychotic symptoms) and F20.2 (catatonic schizophrenia, though less likely given presentation, or indicate a mood disorder with psychotic features). The key distinguishing feature is whether disorganized thinking preceded psychosis (suggesting a primary thought disorder/possible bipolar disorder) or followed it (suggesting primary psychosis).
doctor.question: When you first heard that woman's voice by the kitchen window 11 months ago, at that exact moment, did your mind feel clear and focused, or was it already racing and jumping around the way it does right now?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 3
target_item.manifestation: There was a quieter spell for several weeks when I was sleeping more and not rushing around as much, but I still heard the voice by the kitchen window and believed the agency was watching us.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about the timeline of the psychotic symptoms (hearing the voice) in relation to the manic symptoms (racing thoughts) to determine if the psychotic symptoms occurred in the absence of a major mood episode.

patient.answer:
Well, at that exact moment... I don't think it was racing. Actually, there was a spell for a few weeks right around then where things were quieter. I was sleeping a lot more, and I wasn't rushing around from house to house so much. But even when things were quiet and I was resting, I still heard her voice right there by the kitchen window. I still knew the agency was watching us, even if my thoughts weren't going a mile a minute. 

Speaking of the window, I need to wash it. The glass gets so streaky when it rains. I use vinegar and newspaper to clean the windows at the Hendersons' house, it works much better than that blue spray stuff. My mother taught me that trick. She used to save all the Sunday papers just for cleaning. The Sunday paper used to be so thick, full of coupons and the colored comics. I always read the comics first... Peanuts was my favorite. Snoopy sleeping on top of his doghouse... I never understood how he didn't roll off in his sleep. I toss and turn so much at night, mostly because of my husband's snoring, like I told you. If I slept on a roof, I'd fall right off and break my neck. 

But no, my mind wasn't racing then. It was actually one of those quieter spells, but the voice and the agency watching us... that was all still happening.

doctor.intent: Determine whether the onset of racing thoughts/flight of ideas occurred before, simultaneously with, or after the onset of delusions and hallucinations, to differentiate between F20.0 (paranoid schizophrenia with primary psychotic features) and F20.2 (catatonic schizophrenia or schizophrenia with prominent disorganization)
doctor.question: You've told me that a few weeks after you first heard the woman's voice by the kitchen window, your thoughts started racing really fast. Is that right—the racing thoughts came after the voice started, not before?

target_item.name: Additional Requirement 1
target_item.manifestation: During the weeks when I was sleeping very little and running from cleaning jobs to church errands, I was also hearing that woman's voice and feeling certain people were monitoring my routes.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking to clarify the timeline and overlap of the racing thoughts (manic symptoms) and the voice (psychotic symptoms). This item addresses the concurrent occurrence of both symptom types.

patient.answer:
Yes, that's right. The racing came a bit after. But you know, during those weeks when my thoughts were just flying and I was barely sleeping at all... I was just running constantly, from my cleaning jobs straight to church errands and back again. And the whole time I was rushing around like that, I was still hearing her voice. I was absolutely certain people were monitoring the routes I was taking between the houses and the church. 

I take Elm Street to get to the church usually, because the traffic lights on Main Street take forever. They put in a new light by the old bakery, and it stays red for what feels like hours. I used to love that bakery. They made these little powdered sugar cookies that melted right on your tongue. My aunt used to buy them for my birthday every year. She passed away last spring, bless her heart. We had her funeral at the same church I do the bulletins for. The flowers were beautiful, mostly lilies. I always think lilies smell a bit too sweet, almost like they're trying to cover something up. But they do look nice against the dark wood of the altar. I have to polish that wood next week... 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, yes, the racing thoughts definitely started after the voice. I'm sure of that now.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a clear psychotic disorder with prominent delusions of reference and persecution (belief that hospital/agency personnel are monitoring her house and cleaning routes), combined with auditory hallucinations (hearing a woman's voice by the kitchen window giving commands). Onset was approximately 11 months ago. Critically, the patient demonstrates formal thought disorder with marked tangentiality and flight of ideas that developed after the initial psychotic symptoms emerged. She reports a period of reduced need for sleep concurrent with the racing thoughts and increased goal-directed activity (constant rushing between cleaning jobs and church errands). These features of disorganized speech, reduced sleep need, and increased goal-directed activity occurring alongside psychotic symptoms suggest F20.2 (Catatonic type) is less likely than F20.0 (Paranoid type), but the prominent disorganization and formal thought disorder with some features suggestive of a mixed presentation warrant consideration of this diagnosis. However, the predominance of delusions and hallucinations with secondary disorganization, plus the absence of prominent negative symptoms or catatonic features, most strongly supports F20.2 as the primary diagnosis, with F20.0 as the primary differential.
